name: Coffee Silo Operations - New Orleans LA
type: Distribution/Processing - Green coffee bean silo operations

fieldNotes.location: Silocaf / Smucker Coffee Silo Operations, the world's largest automated green-coffee silo plant, 5240-5242 Coffee Dr. Built ~1992 on the cleared site of the former Public Grain Elevator. Confirmed via satellite: a compact vertical processing building with a row of cylindrical bulk-storage silos along its south edge, conveyors and a blue-roofed annex, sitting inside the Port of New Orleans Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE but indirect — the Silocaf building has no separate fenced perimeter or its own gate. It sits deep inside the secured Port of New Orleans Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal; all truck access is controlled at the port terminal's manned gate. Classified as a controlled (gated) truck entrance at the terminal level. Flagged uncertain because the gate is the port's, not the facility's own.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Marked true — Port of New Orleans container terminals operate manned gatehouses with TWIC/credential checks. Not directly visible in usable imagery (no public Street View inside the secured terminal); inferred from standard port-terminal security practice. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Set true — a port-terminal context typically involves a first checkpoint at the terminal gate, then a separate check-in/transfer point at the Silocaf building itself for bulk-coffee loading/unloading. Two-stage check-in is characteristic; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 0-10 — this is a vertical silo plant, not a flat distribution center. Bulk green coffee moves via hopper trailers, conveyors and pneumatic transfer rather than a long rhythm of dock doors. ~6 transfer/dock points estimated. Flagged low confidence.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 0-10 — a handful of trailers (~8 visible, bulk hopper + box) parked on the west apron; no large marked drop-yard. Capacity ~14.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE — extensive Public Belt / port rail yards run immediately along the north edge; green coffee is moved by rail as well as truck and ship.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Large open paved terminal aprons surround the facility; ample room exists to organize bypass/express lanes for bulk-coffee trucks.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 6.1 acres for the Silocaf building footprint plus its immediate truck apron and silo row. The broader Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal it sits within is far larger but is a separate port property.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: 2 — the main processing/silo building and an adjacent office/ancillary building to the NE.
fieldNotes.confidence: Medium overall — the facility was positively identified and the silo plant is unambiguous, but it is enclosed within a secured port terminal with no public Street View, so gate/guard-shack/lane details are inferred from port-operations context rather than directly observed.

citations.claim: Smucker self-attests 'our three New Orleans facilities' include the largest bulk coffee facility in the world and references 'our Silo facility'.
Listing for 'Smucker Coffee Silo Operations' at 5242 Coffee Dr handling raw green/decaf/soluble coffee through blending and shipment to roasting.

verification.rationale: Despite legacy 'Silocaf/Pacorini' name, current evidence (Smucker Coffee Silo Operations LLC + Smucker green-coffee-ops staffing) shows Smucker-operated today.
